title: Subsets
keyIdea: Backtracking: from start, add each number, recurse with i + 1 (only later numbers, so no order repeats), then remove it. Each call saves its path once: 2ⁿ subsets. Or count a bitmask from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1.

approaches.name: Bitmask
approaches.idea: mask from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1; bit i on → take nums[i].

approaches.name: Backtracking
approaches.idea: solve(start): for i from start: push nums[i], solve(i + 1), pop. After the loop save path.
approaches.why: One call per subset, each copied in O(n).

quiz.q: Why recurse with i + 1 and not 0?
options: Only later numbers may follow, so [1,2] is built and [2,1] never is

quiz.q: How many subsets does a set of n numbers have?
Why pop_back after the recursive call?
options: To undo the choice before trying the next number (backtracking)

quiz.q: In the bitmask version, what does bit i of mask mean?
options: Whether nums[i] is in this subset
